conviction_note: The release's own book line is already published: the Sep-30 NAV estimate of $4.04 and the Oct-31 estimate of $3.85-3.91 (497AD filed 2026-11-18). So the print turns on what management says on the 11-20 call about the November NAV, buybacks under the $20M authorization, and whether the $0.08 monthly distribution (30% of price, about 1.5x the June-quarter NII) survives. At $3.15 the stock sits about 19% below the Oct-31 NAV midpoint, and a cut is largely in the price. The findings net +0.7, a mild lean from the discount and the buyback against distribution-cut risk. p_up 53 x abs 3.5 gives +0.21. The scaled number is smaller than the findings' sum because the two biggest findings (discount and buyback, against the distribution) point in opposite directions and only management's call words resolve them.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-18, the day before the print, EARN published its Oct-31 estimated NAV of $3.85-3.91 (midpoint $3.88, down about 2% after the $0.08 distribution). It traded at $3.48, a 10.3% discount, on Oct-31. At today's $3.15 the discount to that midpoint is about 18.8%, against 0.0% on Sep-30 and a 2.1% premium in July. The stock is priced for a further NAV fall or a distribution cut that no company document has yet shown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 6 of the last 8 prints rose, and the last four all rose (+2.07, +3.23, +2.29, +0.59; baseline). Not tested before from a discount this deep: the fund traded at roughly zero to a small premium until September.
findings.why_not_priced: The NAV estimate is public, but the price has moved about 9.5% below its Oct-31 level while the published NAV fell about 2%. Either the market expects a November NAV drop like ECC's 9% October drop, or a distribution cut. If the market believed the $3.88 held, the discount would sit near the 0-10% band of Sep-Oct rather than at 19%. The call is where management usually gives an updated NAV view.
findings.independence: Sep-30 factsheet at a 0.0% discount (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1560672/000199937126022873/earn-497ad_101626.htm). Price $3.15 from the sealed baseline. Peer ECC trades at a 44% discount to its October NAV (https://finviz.com/news/422707/eagle-point-credit-beats-on-a-one-off-payoff-while-nav-erosion-and-a-bleaker-clo-outlook-dominate), which suggests sector discounts can widen further, a caveat already netted into this size.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 the board authorized repurchases of up to $20M of common shares in the open market through 2027-10-09. That is about 16% of the current $124M market cap (39.5M shares at $3.15), and the fund held $24M of cash at Oct-31. At a roughly 19% discount every repurchase is NAV-accretive. The 11-19 release or the 11-20 call will be the first disclosure of whether any shares were bought; the Oct-31 share count of 39.5M shows none of substance by then.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior EARN buyback disclosure in the baseline window. The stock fell about 15% in the week of the authorization, so the authorization alone did not support it.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public, but whether it is being used is not. If the market expected active repurchases, the discount would not have widened from 10% to 19% in November. A disclosed purchase of several million dollars, or a commitment to buy at this discount, is new information.
findings.independence: Sister REIT EFC, under the same external manager (Ellington), disclosed post-quarter buybacks at about 85% of book on its 2026-11-04 Q3 call (https://finviz.com/news/417482/ellington-financial-misses-as-longbridge-margins-collapse-core-portfolio-holds-firm-but-run-rate-guidance-slips-to-045), a sign that this manager does execute buybacks at discounts. One against this: the 2026-10-23 ATM shows the manager also wants to grow the fund.

findings.finding: The $0.08 monthly distribution ($0.24 a quarter, a 27.6% distribution rate at the Oct-31 price and about 30% at $3.15) runs about 1.5x the June-quarter NII of $0.16 (adjusted $0.15). Peer OXLC halved its monthly distribution on 2026-11-05 as CLO equity cash yields fell from 16.3% to 12.4%. Peer ECC's normalized NII of about $0.18 only equals its payout. A cut or 'reset' signal on the 11-20 call is the main downside path, though EARN re-declared $0.08 for December on 2026-11-05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No EARN distribution change since the CEF conversion within the baseline history. Peer OXLC fell about 25% around its 11-05 cut-and-NAV release (finviz headline tag, period unstated). EARN hit its low of $3.15 on 11-05, the day of OXLC's cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a 30% yield and a 19% discount are what a market expecting a cut looks like, which is why the size is small. What is not priced is the timing and size. A cut signalled on the call lands inside the window, while maintenance plus a coverage plan would be a relief.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-23 EARN put in place a $125M at-the-market common-share program (Citizens JMP, B. Riley, Lucid, Armstrong; up to 2% commission, which the adviser may pay), with proceeds to be deployed into CLOs within about a month. The program is about the fund's entire market cap, but a closed-end fund generally cannot sell common shares below NAV, so at a 19% discount it is unusable. It reads as an overhang and growth-intent signal, not as dilution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock was $3.70 on 2026-10-26 and fell to $3.15 by 11-05 after the ATM was filed; this overlaps the peer selloff, so the move cannot be attributed to the ATM.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month. The call may say whether any shares were sold before the discount opened (the Oct-31 count of 39.5M against about 38.2M at Jun-30 shows issuance happened earlier in the year). The 'cannot sell below NAV' constraint is an inference from the 1940 Act framework, not stated in the documents read.

The run-up is sharply negative (-12% over 20 days, at the 52-week low), and the lean from the deepened discount and buyback goes with a mean-reversion read rather than against any priced statement. lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar, $0.19 against $0.24): the NII-against-consensus finding was capped from -0.4 to -0.3. Findings resting on company NAV documents were left uncapped.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the ATM cannot be used below NAV and has no corroborated use while at a discount, so it was cut from -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 5 (a proxy loses to the company's own number): the ECC/OXLC NAV read-through was cut from -0.5 to -0.3 because EARN's own Oct-31 NAV estimate already exists.
p_up moved from 52 to 53 as the net of the smaller negatives. abs_move_pct was left at 3.5 (above the 2.22 median, for a fund at its low with distribution risk).
Rule 1, rule 7 and rule 8 left everything else standing: misses have not been sold, short interest is not crowded, and there is no confirmed unpriced company number.
